claims.evidence: The witness identified it as a generic 4-cylinder engine; no brand markings or engine codes are visible in the report.
No shipping documents, port clearance papers, or bill of lading shown.
The report describes a static photo; no video of the engine running or compression test results provided.
No odometer reading from the donor vehicle or service history logs.
Requires close-up photos of factory seals and bolt heads on the head/sump to check for tool marks.

risks.proof: A video clip of the engine running with clear audio or a compression test report.
risks.if_unproven: as a non-working core for parts

risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine code stamped on the block (e.g., 5S-FE).
A photo of the underside of the oil filler cap and the visible valvetrain through the filler hole.
risks.if_unproven: as a high-mileage engine requiring internal cleaning

risks.proof: A 360-degree video showing the presence of the alternator, starter, and AC compressor.

proof_requests: Photo of the engine model code stamped on the engine block.
Video of the engine running or a manual crank test to ensure it is not seized.
Photo of the underside of the oil filler cap.
Clear photos of the engine from all four sides to check for leaks and missing parts.
Importation documents (Bill of Lading) to verify 'Tokunbo' status.
response.reason: The witness cannot confirm the specific model or mechanical state. Without the engine code and proof of operation, it cannot be priced even at a worst-case for a specific Camry model.
